strongest_angle: Examining the seven-year legal battle between SoundExchange and Music Choice as the unpaid royalties case resumes in November 2026, including its history dating back to the April 2019 lawsuit and the 2013-2016 audit period.

key_facts.fact: SoundExchange filed the original lawsuit against Music Choice in April 2019, alleging that the company underpaid statutory royalties between 2013 and 2016 for its Music Choice for Business service.
The auditor Prager Metis claimed that Music Choice had concealed the majority of the revenues obtained from the Music Choice for Business subscription service during the 2013 to 2016 period.
The U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit dismissed Music Choice's petition for review in August 2026 concerning a Copyright Royalty Board ruling regarding royalty underpayments.
The marathon legal battle between SoundExchange and Music Choice resumed in November 2026, more than seven years after the initial complaint was filed over unpaid royalties and late fees.

named_entities.name: U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit
